text:
Alex (QuickCart): Hey team — QuickCart saw a sudden flood of 429s around 09:12 UTC. They say it started after a marketing email and lasted ~90s. They pasted a bunch of logs showing burst credits at 0. Can someone explain why the burst buffer emptied so fast?
Maya Chen: Sorry to hear that. Do we have the request pattern? token counts / rps / headers?
Alex (QuickCart): They sent 2,200 requests in ~75s. Mostly small completions (~20 tokens). Header snapshot they sent: `X-Redwood-Burst-Credits: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Reset: 1690000300`. Also `x-request-id: rq_5f1234` in a few samples.
Emma Rivera: thanks. That looks like burst credits drained. Default smoothing window is 60s with a token-bucket that refills at the account rate. If they had a short intense spike over sustained RPS, burst credits will be consumed quickly.
Alex (QuickCart): Is there any automatic smoothing aside from credits? They expected short spikes to be absorbed. This felt abrupt.
Maya Chen: There are two layers: 1) per-second smoothing (very small buffer) and 2) burst credits (larger buffer for short bursts). The burst pool is meant to absorb occasional spikes but isn’t unlimited. If you exceed the combined capacity (bucket + credits) you get 429s.
Akash Patel: @Maya had we logged token-bucket metrics for that account during the interval? I can pull ingress->rate-limiter traces.
Maya Chen: Not yet visible in support logs, requesting from infra. Alex, can you share a sample curl or a safe repro we can run? Prefer sanitized payload.
Alex (QuickCart): Here's a redacted curl they provided that triggers it (they say):
```bash
for i in {1..2200}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-small","input":"ping","max_tokens":20}' &
done
wait
```
They ran that from a single container, concurrent background curls.
John Li: That pattern is basically a fanout spike; 2200 concurrent-ish requests is outside normal smoothing assumptions. Burst credits won't hold for that long. We treat burst credits as short-term absorb for modest bursts (single-digit seconds at high RPS) not multi-minute floods.
Alex (QuickCart): Ok but they say their marketing opens are short bursts — ~1-2 minutes. Curious what settings could help them without upgrading dedicated.
Maya Chen: Options: (a) implement client-side smoothing (throttle back to <200 rps and queue), (b) for hosted customers, we can propose increasing their steady quota (refill rate) or raising allowed burst credits for their account, (c) for high variability use Redwood Dedicated or rate-limited ingress gateway.
Akash Patel: For (b) we need product approval, maybe a temporary buffer increase while they adjust their infra; I'll open a support action to Sales/PM. Also collecting metrics: ingress RPS, token-bucket depletion graph, and backend error tail latency.
Emma Rivera: Also check their response headers from our side — we surface `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-Redwood-Burst-Credits`. If they see `0` for both remaining and burst credits that's definitive. If they have `remaining > 0` but still 429, that's a bug.
Alex (QuickCart): All the samples they pasted show Remaining=0 and Burst-Credits=0.
Maya Chen: Can you ask them for `x-request-id`s of failed samples? We can use those to look up router traces.
Alex (QuickCart): Provided two ids: rq_5f1234 and rq_5f5678.
Akash Patel: grabbing traces now... infra-bot: trace lookup for rq_5f1234 -> rate_limiter: decision=reject reason=burst_exhausted, bucket_state={tokens:0,burst_credits:0}, policy=account-default.
infra-bot: trace lookup for rq_5f5678 -> decision=reject reason=burst_exhausted, bucket_state={tokens:0,burst_credits:0}, refill_rate=1800 tokens/min.
John Li: refill_rate 1800/min ~= 30 tokens/sec. If many concurrent requests consume tokens faster than 30/sec and burst credits are finite, you will get drained. 2200 concurrent small requests will exhaust quickly.
Maya Chen: Repro steps for support to validate environment: 1) Run a controlled spike from a single client as Alex shared (start with 200 concurrent then step up). 2) Capture response headers. 3) If you want to test smoothing change, we can temporarily bump account refill_rate to 3000/min and observe (needs approval).
Alex (QuickCart): They asked about smoothing policies — is there an exponential backoff policy server-side? They expected some auto-smoothing instead of pure rejection.
Emma Rivera: We don't silently queue large numbers of requests because that can increase tail latency for everyone. We do have a soft-smoothing attempt for a few ms, but not for multi-second queuing. Rejection is preferred for predictable SLOs. We offer client-side SDK helpers that implement jittered backoff and queuing.
John Li: For Dedicated customers we can configure ingress LB to provide more aggressive smoothing (larger token bucket and longer short-term queue) because capacity is reserved. For hosted it's constrained by multi-tenant fairness.
Akash Patel: Action items: 1) Maya to request temporary refill increase for QuickCart (Sales+PM signoff). 2) Emma to share SDK guidance + example smoothing code. 3) John to add a short note to runbook about marketing-driven spikes and recommended pre-warm. I'll assign INC-2026-089 for tracking.
Maya Chen: Alex, please tell them to implement client-side queueing as first line mitigation. Here's a small JS example they can drop into their sender: 
```js
// simple token-leaky queue
const queue = [];
let concurrent = 0;
const MAX_CONC = 150; // target smoothing level
async function sendQueued(req) {
  while (concurrent >= MAX_CONC) await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 25));
  concurrent++;
  try { await fetch('/proxy', req); } finally { concurrent--; }
}
```
This lower MAX_CONC dramatically reduces burst consumption of server-side credits.
Alex (QuickCart): Great, will pass along. Anything we should warn customers about in docs?
Emma Rivera: Added a note to the support KB draft: "High-volume short bursts (multi-second, thousands of concurrent requests) may exhaust burst credits quickly; use client-side smoothing or request quota increase pre-campaign." Will link to SDK snippet.
Akash Patel: Follow-up: Maya, once Sales approves, let me know and I’ll temporarily increase account refill rate + burst credits for 1 hour to help them recover. We'll monitor from telemetry.
Maya Chen: Will do. Alex — I'll update this thread when Sales approves. Thanks for the quick repro curl, that made triage much faster. :thumbsup:
